subject: POC load behavior mapping & ops ownership — next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@rapidretail.com>, RapidRetail Infra <infra@rapidretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC load behavior mapping & ops ownership — next steps

Hi Susan / Infra team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to see how RapidRetail's recommendation engine traffic behaves during promos. As promised, here's a concise plan to kick off the POC and what we need from your side to get the trial running in the next two weeks.

Summary of agreed goals (we'll validate these during the POC):
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency < 120ms for 99% of steady-state queries; peak-burst tail latency under 350ms for 30s bursts; no quality regressions vs baseline (CTR impact <= 1.5%).
- Workload profile to reproduce: baseline 120 RPS steady, average token length ~28 tokens, concurrency ~8 workers, bursts up to 1,200 RPS for 20–45s during promotions.
- Evaluation plan: run head-to-head across two model configs (fp16 baseline, quantized 4-bit candidate) for 48h each, capture token-level latency, KV hit rate, and end-to-end request success rate.

What we need from RapidRetail by EOD Thu (2027-05-06):
1) Sample traffic CSV (anonymized) with these columns: timestamp_iso, route, request_tokens, response_tokens, client_region, user_id_hash, qps_bucket. (I attached a small sample template.)
2) A point person for infra/ops who can approve intermittent burst tests and firewall rules: please confirm the contact and their Slack handle.
3) Any hard SLOs for availability or circuit-breaker conditions we should respect.

Redwood deliverables and owners:
- Tessa (me): POC coordinator, timeline/exec updates, success signoff.
- Ben Carter: load harness and traffic replay, test orchestration.
- Karthik Iyer: performance guardrails and quantization candidate validation.
- Dev Patel: runbook for telemetry ingestion and dashboarding.

Attachments: rapidretail_traffic_sample.csv (template), poc-success-metrics.xlsx (metrics matrix), redwood-poc-runbook.pdf (ops checklist).

Proposed timeline:
- 2027-05-06: receive sample traffic + ops contact (RapidRetail)
- 2027-05-09 — 2027-05-13: baseline replay + baseline model run
- 2027-05-14 — 2027-05-18: candidate config run + comparative evaluation
- 2027-05-19: readout and signoff / next steps

If that works, I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff with your infra lead next week.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Susan Park <susan.park@rapidretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: RapidRetail Infra <infra@rapidretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC load behavior mapping & ops ownership — next steps

Thanks Tessa — this is great and lines up with our expectations. A few clarifications from infra: 

- Baseline steady RPS is closer to 100 RPS for the US west region but spikes are highly regionalized; during flash promos the global burst can reach 1,400 RPS for 30s centered on us-west nodes.
- Average request tokens are ~26; some long-form merchant descriptions push the 95th pct to ~110 tokens (rare).
- Concurrency: our API gateway currently allows up to 40 parallel connections per client IP; we typically see 6–10 long-lived connections from the recommendation service.

I'll drop the sample anonymized traffic CSV into the Drive link by EOD Thursday and loop in our infra lead, Mark Lee (mark.lee@rapidretail.com). He'll be the ops approver.

Question: for the quantized candidate, do you expect any change to output determinism that could affect CTR? If so, we'll want to run an A/B on a small % of traffic before broader validation.

-Susan
Susan Park
Head of Personalization | RapidRetail
susan.park@rapidretail.com

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@rapidretail.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC load behavior mapping & ops ownership — next steps

Hi Susan — thanks for the numbers, very helpful. A couple of practical notes from the test harness side: 

- We'll run localized burst profiles against a us-west replica first to limit blast radius. We can parameterize bursts in the harness as: baseline_rps=100, burst_peak=1400, burst_duration=30s, inter-burst-interval=12m.
- For token distributions, please include the 5th/50th/95th token-length percentiles if possible — makes kernel selection far more accurate.
- We will instrument the replay with the following telemetry (each line in the CSV will be mapped to): request_id, replay_start, request_latency_ms, model_token_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio, status_code.

Operational asks:
- Ideally we'll get a service-account API key with a scoped replay endpoint for the window 2027-05-09 to 2027-05-18. If not, we can replay from our harness against a staging proxy you provide.

I'll prepare the harness config and attach here once ready.

Ben Carter
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

(attachment: none)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@rapidretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC load behavior mapping & ops ownership — next steps

Hi all,

Quick note on telemetry and dashboards: please confirm the preferred format for token-level telemetry. We support two ingestion formats out of the box:
- Line-delimited CSV as Ben outlined (request_id, replay_start, request_latency_ms, model_token_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio, status_code) — simplest for replays.
- JSONL with additional context (route, client_region, features) — preferred if you have user features we should correlate to latency/quality.

Also: the runbook I'll publish (redwood-poc-runbook.pdf) includes circuit-breaker thresholds; let us know if any of those need to match internal RapidRetail SRE rules.

I'll upload a first-pass harness config and a small replay manifest tonight to the Drive link so you can review.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

(attachment: rapidretail_traffic_sample.csv - anonymized sample filled by RapidRetail template)

From: Susan Park <susan.park@rapidretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Lee <mark.lee@rapidretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC load behavior mapping & ops ownership — next steps

All,

I've uploaded the anonymized traffic CSV to the Drive folder (link above) and confirmed Mark Lee as the infra approver (Slack: @mark-lee). Link includes the 5/50/95 token percentiles and region tags.

We agree to the A/B approach for the quantized candidate — we'll start at 2% traffic after the candidate run looks stable in replay. If CTR drift exceeds 0.8% at 95% confidence, we'll stop and discuss rollbacks.

Mark, please let the Redwood team know when you're available for a 30-min kickoff next week. Tessa, if you can send a calendar invite with an agenda (30m): objectives, success criteria, telemetry format, and kickoff runbook — we'll accept.

Thanks,

Susan Park
Head of Personalization | RapidRetail
susan.park@rapidretail.com
